extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of systematic philosophy/metaphysics (readers of Schopenhauer)
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a 19th-century metaphysical work arguing that 'will' is the thing-in-itself and describing how manifestations of will appear across plant, animal, and unorganised nature. Contains normative claims about explanation, genius, and standards for scientific and poetic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of intellect from will as measure of intellectual completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: In proportion as, in the ascending series of animals, the intellect appears ever more developed and complete, knowledge always separates itself more distinctly from will, and thereby becomes purer. Upon the degree of this separation ultimately depends the difference and the gradation of intellectual capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains grading from plants (will manifesting as reproductive power without knowledge) through animals (intellect fused with will) to humans (greater separation). Uses physiological development of nervous/muscular systems to ground this criterion: more separation → greater objectivity of perception and higher intellectual capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity of knowledge as a scale (genius as its apex)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectivity of knowledge, and primarily of perceptive knowledge, has innumerable grades ... the highest of which is genius, in which the comprehension of the external world becomes so pure and objective that to it even more reveals itself directly in the individual thing than the individual thing itself, namely, the nature of its whole species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines genius as the condition of perfectly will-less, completely objective knowledge. The criterion for evaluating levels of cognition or aesthetic comprehension is the degree to which the will is absent from consciousness and knowledge appears purely objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genius defined by will-lessness and species comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius may be defined as the highest grade of the objectivity of knowledge ... in this case the will entirely vanishes from consciousness ... the free surplus which first really properly comes to know the world ... comprehends it perfectly objectively, and now paints pictures, composes poems, and thinks in accordance with this comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing artistic or intellectual achievement, check whether the creator manifests a 'will-less' contemplative perception that grasps the Platonic Idea/species of things rather than merely individual motives or utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness to laws of nature as criterion for literary fame
rubrics_metrics.description: The more correctly, the more strictly according to the laws of nature his characters are there presented, the greater is his fame; hence Shakespeare stands at the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For drama, epic, or romance, evaluate how faithfully characters' conduct and suffering conform to natural laws of human will and motive. Greater fidelity yields greater lasting reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of will without knowledge (plant life)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the plant possesses neither irritability nor sensibility, but the will objectifies itself in it only as plastic or reproductive power, it has neither muscle nor nerve ... in the life of plants the truth that will can exist without knowledge is apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When attributing intentional-like behaviour to organisms, look for adaptive, goal-directed changes determined by wants (nutrition, reproduction) even in the absence of perceptual knowledge or nervous apparatus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organised vs unorganised criterion for life/organism
rubrics_metrics.description: In the unorganised body that which is essential and permanent is the material; with the organised body the case is exactly reversed; its life consists in the constant change of the material, while the form remains permanent ... the predicate life belongs only to what is organised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To judge whether something is an organism, require pervasive internal organisation (form persistent across material turnover). Reject attributions of 'life' to wholly unorganised aggregates (e.g., the globe) unless all parts are organised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Will as metaphysical foundation of natural forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The will ... is the prius of knowledge, the kernel of our nature, and that original force itself which forms and sustains the animal body ... it is the thing in itself so far as this can ever be reached by knowledge. Consequently it is that which must express itself in some way in everything in the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative principle for metaphysics and explanation: seek the 'will' as the inner nature grounding forces of plants, animals, crystals, gravity, etc. Use organismal and physical phenomena as evidential parallels to one's own inner will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forces of nature lie outside the chain of causes and effects (eternity/ideality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The forces of nature lie outside the chain of causes and effects, because they constitute their accompanying condition, their metaphysical foundation, and therefore prove themselves to be eternal and omnipresent, i.e. independent of time and space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing claims about natural laws, treat forces as metaphysically primary and timeless; empirical causal chains do not exhaust explanation—metaphysics must 'take up the thread where physics leaves it' at original forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical explanations limited; prefer dynamical explanations for many phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: We have a natural inclination whenever it is possible to explain every natural phenomenon mechanically ... However ... the application of mechanical explanatory hypotheses, beyond what is demonstrably mechanical, is entirely unjustified ... light, heat, and electricity ... will always admit only of a dynamical explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scientific theories by whether their explanatory mode is appropriate: accept mechanical explanations only where demonstrably mechanical (e.g., some mechanics); require dynamical (original force-based) explanations for chemical combinations, aggregation states, and phenomena like light and heat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting physical behaviour as manifestations of will (self-preservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If we consider the will, where no one denies it, in conscious beings, we find everywhere, as its fundamental effort, the self-preservation of every being ... here also the seeking shows itself as gravitation, and the shunning as the receiving of motion ... movableness of bodies ... is at bottom a manifestation of the effort after self-preservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the teleological notion of self-preservation to read mechanical phenomena (e.g., elasticity, pressure response, gravitation) as expressions of will. This supplies a criterion for interpreting physical regularities as analogues of volitional behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallisation and quasi-life as evidence of will in unorganised nature
rubrics_metrics.description: In the forming of the crystal we see, as it were, a tendency towards an attempt at life, to which, however, it does not attain ... only the trace remains as the crystal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating borderline cases between organised and unorganised, regard structured growth (crystallisation) as a faint manifestation or 'trace' of will—a quasi-life—rather than full organismic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for assessing physical theories: avoid hidden mechanistic dogma
rubrics_metrics.description: Those constructions of light from molecules and atoms which have originated with the French are indeed a revolting absurdity ... At bottom they are still Lockeians ... matter must be ultimately explicable. They will not let themselves be talked out of this, and their tacit assumption is that matter can only be moved by mechanical forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess scientific doctrines by whether they covertly presuppose mechanical atomism without metaphysical warrant. The presence of such tacit mechanistic assumptions is a mark against their plausibility in favour of dynamical/metaphysical accounts.
